LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DETERMINERS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are articles used with nouns?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication
2. use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DETERMINERS
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 1.3.1 WORD CLASSES: DETERMINERS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners to a partner. (skill: use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are articles used with nouns?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify definite and indefinite articles in a written text for effective communication.
5. Be able to: use definite and indefinite articles in sentences for effective communication.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
